purpose: How to judge and validate a grade for a browser-rendered export. Shot-specific numbers never transfer between setups; redo the checks for each new camera, lighting or renderer.
source_checks: Read camera gamma/gamut, matrix and range metadata; confirm S-Log3/S-Gamut3.Cine input
Inspect original 10-bit source before judging clipped exports

Inspect available source highlight gradation before the output transform; do not promise missing detail can be recovered. The V3 extra highlight curve was rejected and is not part of the current C baseline.
scope_checks: Use luma waveform for brightness, highlights and flat clipped plateaus
Use RGB parade and credible neutral references for channel imbalance, without flattening intentional coloured lighting
Isolate un-bearded skin patches for vectorscope inspection; treat skin indicator as hue guidance, not an exact target or universal skin brightness

Inspect early, middle and late shots; verify export primaries, matrix, range, transfer and true peaks against the actual image encoding, then compare a matched preview frame through the intended player.
shot_specific: Do not reuse correction numbers blindly across new lighting/camera setups

export_validation.principle: Do not approve colour from ffprobe tags or FFmpeg pixel decoding alone. Compare the exact preview and exported frame through a colour-managed playback path.
export_validation.workflow_specific: HyperFrames 0.9.19 browser capture in this project produces sRGB-coded RGB. Tested Apple AVFoundation/CoreGraphics playback matches that preview substantially better with transfer 13 in BOTH H.264 VUI and MP4 container. Keep BT709 primaries/matrix and limited YUV range.
export_validation.not_universal: Do not reinterpret camera originals or arbitrary Rec709 masters as sRGB. Revalidate whenever renderer, encoding, source pipeline or target platform changes.
export_validation.lossless_intermediate: Use --video-frame-format png for the delivery render.

how_to_apply_a_grade: Create a HyperFrames media-treatment payload (npx hyperframes media-treatment --help) and save it as work/<video>/color/selected-payload.json; npm run build applies it to #footage.
